practiceQuestions.q: Which Article of the Constitution of India provides for the superintendence, direction, and control of elections to be vested in an Election Commission?
practiceQuestions.sol: Article 324 of the Constitution vests the superintendence, direction, and control of the preparation of the electoral rolls for, and the conduct of, all elections to Parliament and to the Legislature of every State and of elections to the offices of President and Vice-President held under this Constitution in an Election Commission.

practiceQuestions.q: Universal Adult Franchise for elections to the Lok Sabha and the Legislative Assemblies of States in India is enshrined in which Article?
practiceQuestions.sol: Article 326 provides that elections to the House of the People and to the Legislative Assemblies of States shall be on the basis of adult suffrage, meaning that every person who is a citizen of India and is not less than 18 years of age is entitled to be registered as a voter.

practiceQuestions.q: By which Constitutional Amendment Act was the voting age in India reduced from 21 years to 18 years?
practiceQuestions.sol: The 61st Constitutional Amendment Act, 1989 lowered the voting age from 21 years to 18 years by amending Article 326 of the Constitution.

practiceQuestions.q: Article 325 of the Indian Constitution prohibits inclusion in or exclusion from electoral rolls on grounds of which of the following?
opts: Religion, race, caste, sex, descent, place of birth or residence
Religion, race, caste, sex or language
practiceQuestions.sol: Article 325 states that there shall be one general electoral roll for every territorial constituency for election to Parliament and State Legislatures and no person shall be ineligible for inclusion in any such roll or claim to be included in a special electoral roll on grounds only of religion, race, caste, or sex.

practiceQuestions.q: Under which Article of the Constitution does Parliament have the power to make provision with respect to all matters relating to elections to legislatures?
practiceQuestions.sol: Article 327 empowers Parliament to make provision with respect to all matters relating to, or in connection with, elections to either House of Parliament or to the House or either House of the Legislature of a State, including the preparation of electoral rolls and delimitation of constituencies.

practiceQuestions.q: Which of the following best describes the legal nature of the 'Right to Vote' in India?
opts: Constitutional Right under Article 326 and Statutory Right
Natural Right independent of state laws
practiceQuestions.sol: The right to vote in India is rooted in the Constitution (Article 326 grants adult suffrage) and is further operationalized as a statutory right under the Representation of the People Act, 1951. While the Supreme Court has often termed it a constitutional right, it is subject to statutory regulations (like disqualifications, registration requirements).

practiceQuestions.q: When was the Election Commission of India originally established as a multi-member or single-member body?
opts: Body appointed directly by the Prime Minister
practiceQuestions.sol: The Election Commission was established on January 25, 1950. It functioned as a single-member body consisting of only the Chief Election Commissioner until October 16, 1989, when two additional Election Commissioners were appointed for the first time.

practiceQuestions.q: Which Article bars interference by courts in electoral matters?
practiceQuestions.sol: Article 329 bars interference by courts in electoral matters. It states that the validity of any law relating to the delimitation of constituencies or the allotment of seats shall not be called in question in any court, and no election to Parliament or State Legislature shall be called in question except by an election petition.

practiceQuestions.q: What is the tenure of office for the Chief Election Commissioner and Election Commissioners?
opts: 5 years or 65 years of age, whichever is earlier
6 years or 65 years of age, whichever is earlier
During the pleasure of the President
practiceQuestions.sol: According to Article 324(2) and the rules made thereunder, the CEC and Election Commissioners hold office for a term of six years or until they attain the age of 65 years, whichever is earlier.

practiceQuestions.q: Which Act enacted by Parliament provides detailed provisions regarding the registration of electors and conduct of elections?
opts: Representation of the People Act, 1950 and 1951
practiceQuestions.sol: The Representation of the People Act, 1950 provides for the allocation of seats and delimitation of constituencies for elections, and the qualification of voters. The Representation of the People Act, 1951 deals with the actual conduct of elections, administrative machinery, qualifications/disqualifications for membership, and corrupt practices.

practiceQuestions.q: How did the introduction of Universal Adult Franchise in India fundamentally transform its socio-political landscape at the dawn of independence?
opts: It immediately eliminated all forms of socio-economic inequality and caste hierarchy.
It bridged the elite-mass divide by granting equal political weight to every adult citizen regardless of property, literacy, or wealth.
It restricted voting exclusively to educated urban property owners to ensure stable administration.
It delegated all electoral powers entirely to village panchayats without central oversight.
practiceQuestions.sol: Universal Adult Franchise was a bold, revolutionary step in a newly independent, largely poor, and illiterate nation. By granting every adult equal voting rights, it challenged deep-seated feudal hierarchies and empowered marginalized communities, asserting the principle of political equality.

practiceQuestions.q: What is the constitutional significance of having a single integrated electoral roll for both Parliamentary and State Assembly elections under Article 325?
opts: It reduces administrative expenditure for state governments.
It reinforces Indian federalism by ensuring that citizenship of India is the sole criterion for inclusion, preventing states from creating separate discriminatory voter qualifications.
It allows the Election Commission to bypass Parliament during election scheduling.
It makes the judiciary directly responsible for verifying voter lists.
practiceQuestions.sol: Article 325 mandates a single general electoral roll for every territorial constituency, prohibiting separate rolls on grounds of religion, race, caste, or sex. This prevents states from introducing parochial or discriminatory criteria and underscores the unity of Indian citizenship.

practiceQuestions.q: Why does the Constitution separate the removal procedure of the Chief Election Commissioner from that of other Election Commissioners?
opts: To give the CEC absolute autocratic control over the other commissioners.
To guarantee institutional independence; the CEC can be removed only like a Supreme Court judge, whereas other commissioners can be removed on the CEC's recommendation.
Because other commissioners are political appointees of the ruling party.
To allow the Prime Minister to dismiss any commissioner at will.
practiceQuestions.sol: Article 324(5) ensures that the CEC is insulated from executive pressure by providing security of tenure similar to a Supreme Court judge (impeachment-style removal). However, other Election Commissioners can be removed by the President upon the recommendation of the CEC to balance institutional harmony while protecting the Chief's primacy.

practiceQuestions.q: How does the principle of Universal Adult Franchise intersect with the disqualifications for voting outlined under statutory laws like the RP Act, 1951?
opts: Statutory laws can override the constitutional right to vote by denying franchise based on gender.
Universal suffrage is the baseline constitutional norm, but reasonable statutory restrictions can be imposed on grounds of non-residence, unsoundness of mind, crime, or corrupt practices.
Disqualifications can be arbitrarily decided by local police stations without legislative backing.
Statutory laws have completely nullified Article 326 in modern times.
practiceQuestions.sol: While Article 326 establishes universal adult suffrage as a fundamental democratic rule, it explicitly permits Parliament to make laws disqualifying voters on grounds such as non-residence, unsoundness of mind, crime, or corrupt/illegal practices.

practiceQuestions.q: What is the primary rationale behind vesting the power of superintendence and conduct of elections in an independent body like the Election Commission rather than the executive government?
opts: To ensure free, fair, and impartial elections free from executive manipulation or partisan bias.
To make the election machinery completely unaccountable to Parliament.
To ensure that the ruling party directly dictates constituency boundaries.
To reduce voter turnout and streamline administrative paperwork.
practiceQuestions.sol: An independent Election Commission is a cornerstone of Indian democracy. By insulating the electoral process from political and executive interference, Article 324 ensures that elections are conducted fairly, safeguarding the integrity of Universal Adult Franchise.

practiceQuestions.q: How does the Representation of the People Act, 1950 contribute to the operationalization of Universal Adult Franchise?
opts: By laying down the mechanics for the preparation and revision of electoral rolls and seat allocation across constituencies.
By defining criminal penalties for electoral malpractices during vote counting.
By establishing the financial budget of political parties.
By fixing the salaries of High Court judges handling election petitions.
practiceQuestions.sol: The RP Act, 1950 provides the legal framework for seat allocation in Parliament and State Assemblies and sets forth the rules for preparing electoral rolls, ensuring that every eligible citizen under Article 326 can be registered.

practiceQuestions.q: Why is the independence of the Election Commission considered a basic structure of the Constitution?
opts: Because free and fair elections are the bedrock of democracy, which requires an impartial umpire.
Because the Election Commission can amend any part of the Constitution independently.
Because its members are appointed exclusively by civil society organizations.
Because it holds veto power over judicial pronouncements.
practiceQuestions.sol: In various landmark judgments, the Supreme Court has ruled that free and fair elections conducted by an independent body are an essential part of the 'basic structure' of the Indian Constitution, as democracy is rendered meaningless without a credible electoral process.

practiceQuestions.q: What distinguishes the constitutional status of the Election Commission from statutory bodies like the National Human Rights Commission?
opts: The Election Commission is directly created by an Article of the Constitution (Article 324), whereas NHRC is created by an Act of Parliament.
NHRC has judicial powers, while the Election Commission has none.
The Election Commission reports directly to the Prime Minister, unlike NHRC.
There is no functional difference; both are constitutional bodies.
practiceQuestions.sol: Constitutional bodies derive their powers and authority directly from the text of the Constitution (like Article 324 for ECI), making them immune to abolition or alteration through ordinary legislative acts. Statutory bodies are established through legislation enacted by Parliament.

practiceQuestions.q: How does Article 328 operate in the context of federal election governance in India?
opts: It gives State Legislatures the power to make provisions with respect to elections to such legislatures, subject to the provisions of any law made by Parliament.
It allows states to conduct Presidential elections independently.
It empowers Governors to suspend the Election Commission within their state.
It grants absolute autonomy to states to decide voting age independently.
practiceQuestions.sol: Article 328 allows a State Legislature to make laws regarding elections to the state legislature in matters not covered by parliamentary legislation, ensuring a cooperative federal approach under central paramountcy.

practiceQuestions.q: What is the primary significance of the bar under Article 329(b) preventing courts from interfering in elections except through an election petition?
opts: To prevent endless judicial litigation from halting or delaying the democratic electoral process once it has been set in motion.
To give complete immunity to corrupt candidates from any legal accountability.
To abolish the Supreme Court's power of judicial review entirely.
To allow the Election Commission to overrule Supreme Court verdicts on civil rights.
practiceQuestions.sol: The Supreme Court has interpreted Article 329(b) to mean that once an election process has started, it should not be halted by interim court injunctions. Disputes must be resolved post-election via an election petition to ensure timely completion of democratic exercises.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the Election Commission of India:
1. The Election Commission is a permanent and independent body established by the Constitution of India.
2. Article 324 of the Constitution provides for the composition and appointment of members of the Election Commission.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is correct: ECI is a permanent constitutional body created under Article 324. Statement 2 is incorrect because while Article 324 mentions the superintendence and setting up of the Commission and the Chief Election Commissioner, the detailed rules regarding the appointment process, tenure conditions, etc., are left to be determined by laws made by Parliament (and do not detail the entire appointment committee structure directly in Article 324).

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding Universal Adult Franchise in India:
1. The Constitution of India introduced Universal Adult Franchise right from its commencement on January 26, 1950.
2. India was among the first major democracies to grant universal adult suffrage to all citizens without any gender, property, or educational qualifications upon independence.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Both statements are correct. Article 326 established universal adult franchise at the commencement of the Constitution. Unlike Western democracies where women and property-less classes fought prolonged battles for franchise, India boldly granted it to all adult citizens simultaneously.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding Article 325:
1. It provides for a single general electoral roll for every territorial constituency.
2. It allows states to maintain separate communal electorates if approved by a two-thirds majority in the State Legislature.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is correct: Article 325 mandates a single general electoral roll for every territorial constituency. Statement 2 is entirely incorrect; Article 325 explicitly prohibits separate communal electorates and bars any discrimination in electoral rolls on grounds of religion, race, caste, or sex.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the Right to Vote in India:
1. The right to vote is a Fundamental Right guaranteed under Article 19(1)(a) of the Constitution.
2. The Supreme Court of India has held that the right to vote is both a constitutional right and a statutory right.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is incorrect: The Supreme Court has repeatedly clarified that the right to vote is not a fundamental right under Article 19(1)(a) (freedom of speech and expression), but rather a statutory and constitutional right. Statement 2 is correct, as it stems from Article 326 and is regulated by the RP Acts.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the composition and removal of the Election Commission:
1. The Election Commission consists of the Chief Election Commissioner and such number of other Election Commissioners, if any, as the President may from time to time fix.
2. The Chief Election Commissioner can be removed from office only through a process of impeachment similar to that of a judge of the Supreme Court.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Both statements are correct. Article 324(2) empowers the President to fix the number of Election Commissioners. Article 324(5) prescribes that the CEC shall not be removed from office except in like manner and on the like grounds as a judge of the Supreme Court.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the 61st Constitutional Amendment Act, 1989:
1. It amended Article 326 of the Constitution.
2. It reduced the voting age for Lok Sabha and State Legislative Assembly elections from 21 years to 18 years.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Both statements are correct. The 61st Amendment Act, 1989 explicitly amended Article 326 to lower the voting age from 21 to 18, reflecting a massive expansion of democratic participation for India's youth.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding Parliament's power over elections:
1. Article 327 gives Parliament exclusive power to make provisions with respect to all matters relating to elections to Parliament and State Legislatures.
2. State Legislatures have no power whatsoever to legislate on any electoral matter under any circumstance.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is correct: Article 327 empowers Parliament to legislate on all election-related matters. Statement 2 is incorrect because Article 328 explicitly gives State Legislatures the power to make provisions with respect to elections to their own legislatures in matters not covered by parliamentary law.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the powers and functions of the Election Commission:
1. The Election Commission conducts elections to the offices of the President and Vice-President of India.
2. The Election Commission is also responsible for conducting elections to panchayats and municipalities in the states.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is correct: Article 324 assigns the ECI responsibility for Presidential and Vice-Presidential elections alongside Parliament and State Legislatures. Statement 2 is incorrect because elections to panchayats and municipalities are conducted by the respective State Election Commissions created under Articles 243K and 243ZA, not the Election Commission of India.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding Article 329:
1. It bars courts from questioning the validity of any law relating to the delimitation of constituencies or allotment of seats.
2. It permits any voter to challenge an election result directly through a writ petition in the Supreme Court at any stage of the polling process.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is correct: Article 329(a) bars courts from reviewing laws regarding delimitation or seat allotment. Statement 2 is incorrect because Article 329(b) explicitly bars interference during the polling process and stipulates that elections can only be challenged via an election petition presented to such authority as Parliament may establish.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the conditions of service and tenure of Election Commissioners:
1. The conditions of service and tenure of office of the Election Commissioners and Regional Commissioners are determined by the President.
2. An Election Commissioner or a Regional Commissioner can be removed from office upon the recommendation of the Chief Election Commissioner.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Both statements are correct according to Article 324(5). While the President determines the conditions of service and tenure subject to laws made by Parliament, other commissioners cannot be removed except upon the recommendation of the Chief Election Commissioner.
